extraction.name: Video-MME
extraction.description: Video-MME is the first-ever comprehensive Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark of MLLMs in Video analysis, designed to assess the performance of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in video understanding tasks. It features diversity in video types (6 primary visual domains with 30 subfields), temporal duration (ranging from 11 seconds to 1 hour), data modalities (video frames, subtitles, and audios), and high-quality manual annotations by expert annotators. The benchmark includes 900 videos and 2,700 multiple-choice QA pairs, enabling robust evaluation of MLLMs' capabilities in perception, reasoning, and information synthesis across varied scenarios.
extraction.creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
extraction.citeAs: Video-MME: The First-Ever Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark of Multi-modal LLMs in Video Analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset construction involved three main steps: video collection, question-answer annotation, and quality review. Videos were sourced from YouTube across 6 key domains (Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Artistic Performance, Life Record, and Multilingual) with 30 fine-grained categories. Each video was manually reviewed to ensure quality, and QA pairs were created by expert annotators with strong English proficiency and research experience in vision-language learning. The process included a rigorous review to verify clarity, answerability, and reliance on video content.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Videos were collected from YouTube across 6 primary visual domains with 30 subfields, including Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Artistic Performance, Life Record, and Multilingual. The dataset includes 900 videos, 744 with subtitles, and all 900 with audios.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos were curated to ensure diversity in types, durations, and modalities. Subtitles and audios were synchronized with video frames for evaluation. Frame extraction was standardized (e.g., 1 frame per second for short/medium videos, 1 frame every 2 seconds for long videos for Gemini 1.5 Pro; other models followed official guidelines with fixed frame counts). Subtitles corresponding to sampled frames were selected for synchronized multimodal input.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: High-quality question-answer (QA) pairs were manually annotated by expert annotators with strong English proficiency and research experience in vision-language learning. Each annotator created three relevant questions per video, each with four candidate options, resulting in 2,700 QA pairs. The QA pairs were designed to require direct reference to video content, and a rigorous review process ensured clarity, answerability, and reliance on video content.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A quality review process was conducted where each QA pair was examined by a different annotator to verify clarity, answerability, and logical consistency. Additionally, text-only questions were provided to Gemini 1.5 Pro to filter out QA pairs that could be answered without video content, ensuring robustness. Statistical analysis showed Gemini 1.5 Pro achieved less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup, underscoring the reliance on video content.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators were recruited with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning. Specific demographics are not provided in the paper.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark highlights the need for further improvements in handling longer sequences and multimodal data, shedding light on future MLLM development. It underscores the importance of addressing performance declines in long-duration videos and the potential of subtitles and audio to enhance video understanding.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset spans 6 primary visual domains with 30 subfields to ensure broad scenario generalizability, but specific biases are not explicitly discussed in the paper.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include a decline in MLLM performance as video duration increases, indicating challenges in processing longer sequences. The dataset may not fully capture all real-world scenarios, and the reliance on manual annotations could introduce subjectivity. Non-recommended uses include generalizing results to domains not covered by the 6 primary visual domains.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Benchmarking. The dataset is designed for evaluating MLLMs' capabilities in video understanding, including perception, reasoning, and information synthesis. It serves as a universal benchmark for both image and video MLLMs, enabling comprehensive assessment across varied scenarios and temporal durations.
